newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Dow dip drives Australian stocks to lower close.
newsitem.headline: Dow dip drives Australian stocks to lower close.

text.p: The Australian share market closed lower on Friday after Wall Street tumbled with only an heroic performance from National Australia Bank, buoyed by Thursday's first quarter profit, preventing further losses.
The All Ordinaries index fell 11.5 points to 2,423.0.
Brokers said the fall was no surprise given the Dow's showing. National Australia Bank was the only real positive news among the leaders although the smaller end did see some action.
"With the Dow down 90, we have seen a kneejerk reaction which is not surprising," said head of equities at Intersuisse, Andrew Sekely.

National Australia Bank shares streaked ahead again, closing 1.7 percent higher at A$15.78 (US$12.21) after reaching a record high of A$15.93, as investors expressed their approval of Thursday's A$582 milion first quarter net profit result.
"It's a great performance by an unusually well-managed bank," Sekely said.

Featuring at the smaller end was Gawler Craton gold explorer, Desertstone, whose shares spiked 42 percent higher to 85 cents as traders punted on its Lake Torrens prospect before easing back as profit takers emerged.
Desertstone scrip closed three cents higher at A$0.63.
Falls outnumbered rises by a ratio of about three to two, while about 28 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
